title: EFC — Formal Specification
description: This paper presents the formal mathematical specification of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC). It defines the entropy field S(x), the energy–flow field Ef(x), an entropy-coupled effective potential Φ(Ef, S), and an entropy-dependent effective light speed c(S), showing how rotation curves, light-travel times, and lensing emerge from their coupling.

entropy_midpoint_and_span.description: Defines the midpoint and span of the entropy domain.

normalized_entropy_coordinate.description: Dimensionless coordinate that normalizes S to the interval [-1, 1].

effective_light_speed.description: Entropy-dependent effective speed of light; minimal at mid-entropy and enhanced toward both endpoints.

effective_potential.description: Baseline coupling of the energy–flow field and entropy to produce the effective potential.

circular_velocity.description: Rotation-curve relation from the radial gradient of the effective potential.

light_travel_time.description: Observed photon travel time along trajectory \gamma using the entropy-dependent propagation law.

key_results.main_finding: Provides a self-contained formalism in which dynamics and observables co-emerge from an entropy field via Φ(Ef, S) and an entropy-dependent propagation law c(S).

sealed_predictions.statement: The effective photon propagation speed is minimal in mid-entropy environments and increases toward both low-entropy/high-structure (S → S0) and high-entropy (S → S1) regimes, producing systematic shifts in strong-lensing time delays at fixed mass models.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Comparative strong-lensing time-delay measurements across environments with matched lens mass reconstructions; absence of any environment-correlated time-delay residuals would falsify this.

sealed_predictions.statement: A mid-entropy minimum in c(S) yields a stability band for halo-like configurations and naturally flat rotation curves without adding dark components.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision rotation curves across diverse environments that cannot be reproduced using v(r) = sqrt(r ∂r Φ(Ef, S)) with a shared functional form and consistent (A_Φ, a_edge, S0, S1, c0) across systems.

sealed_predictions.statement: Entropy-dependent propagation implies that redshift–distance relations and lensing magnifications depend on S(x); lines of sight traversing endpoint-like regions exhibit faster effective propagation than mid-entropy lines of sight.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Standard-candle/standard-siren Hubble diagrams and lensing magnification statistics conditioned on environmental entropy proxies; null dependence would refute the prediction.

kill_criteria: KC1: Joint analyses of strong-lensing time delays, standard sirens, and standard candles find no measurable environmental dependence of photon (and GW) travel times, constraining a_edge ≈ 0 across the full x(S) range at ≲1% precision.

KC2: The functional pair Φ(E_f, S) = A_Φ E_f (1 + S) and c(S) = c_0 (1 + a_edge x(S)^2) cannot simultaneously account for galaxy rotation curves and lensing observables across systems without object-specific parameter tuning.

KC3: Laboratory, Solar-System, or astrophysical tests bound any effective light-speed variation to be zero independent of environment at levels incompatible with the nonzero a_edge required by EFC phenomenology.
KC4: Empirical mappings of entropy proxies S(x) show that regions near S0 or S1 do not exhibit the predicted enhanced propagation relative to mid-entropy paths, contradicting the edge-enhanced c(S).
KC5: The coupled equations produce unphysical behavior (e.g., negative or imaginary c(S) or v(r)) within observationally required ranges of S, indicating internal inconsistency of the baseline model.
